name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira holds near a record 50 per dollar; no major EM default or capital controls
state: The Turkish lira traded near a record low of 50 per dollar on 3 Nov under a managed depreciation, after the central bank cut its policy rate by 100bp to 36% and October inflation rose to 29.8% (Trading Economics; Shafaq News). The slide is gradual, not a 10% monthly fall, and no major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF help as of 6 Nov.
for_you: A weaker lira raises import costs in Turkey and makes holidays there cheaper for visitors. Wider emerging-market stress has not spread.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month, default or capital controls (Normal)

sources.title: Trading Economics — Turkish lira holds at record lows
Shafaq News — Turkish lira breaches 50 per dollar to record low

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
